name: 20-20-20 look-away
instruction: Look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds
why: gives your eyes a short screen break

name: Palming
instruction: Rub your palms together to warm them, then gently cup them over your closed eyes without pressing on the eyeballs until things fade to black
why: gives eyes a short rest from screen focus

name: Near-far focus shift
instruction: Hold one thumb near your face and focus on it, then shift focus to something farther away, then something across the room, then something even farther; about 2 seconds each
why: exercises the eyes' ability to change focus, which screen use limits
restrictions: not a substitute for professional eye care if you have a diagnosed vision condition

name: Shoulder rolls
instruction: Gently roll shoulders 3 times forward and 3 times back
why: changes position and moves the shoulders

name: Chin tuck
instruction: Gently tuck your chin and draw your head straight back, without looking up or down, until you feel a stretch
why: counters the forward-head posture screen use encourages

name: Side neck stretch
instruction: Sit or stand tall, bring one arm gently over your head with your hand on the opposite side of your head, and pull your head toward that shoulder without turning or tilting
why: releases one-sided tension from screen/mouse position
restrictions: ease off if it worsens symptoms

name: Hand open/close
instruction: Gently make a fist, then open the hand and spread the fingers; repeat 3 times

name: Wrist side-to-side bend
instruction: With fingers and wrist straight, gently bend your wrist first toward your little finger, then toward your thumb
why: moves the wrist through range typing and mousing miss

name: Hook fist to full fist
instruction: Keeping your knuckles straight, bend your fingers into a hook fist, then roll your fingers into your palm to make a full fist
why: moves the finger tendons through their full range

name: Slouch to tall
instruction: While seated, gently slouch, then sit tall; repeat 3 times
why: changes the sitting position and gently moves the lower back
restrictions: omit for back pain/limits or uncertainty

name: Standing back extension
instruction: Standing with knees slightly bent, place your hands on your lower back and gently lean back while pushing your hands forward
why: counters the forward-flexed spine position of sitting
restrictions: stop if pain; standing must be allowed

name: Cat stretch
instruction: On hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, slowly round your back upward letting your head relax forward, then slowly reverse, letting your spine sink
why: gently mobilizes the spine after sitting still

name: Stand and walk
instruction: Stand and walk near the desk for 60 seconds
why: breaks up a long period of sitting

name: Wall press-up
instruction: Stand facing a wall, hands shoulder-width apart with fingers pointing up; bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then straighten your arms back out
why: brief upper-body strength break from sitting

name: Standing thigh stretch
instruction: Stand next to a wall or chair for support, bend your knee, grip your ankle, and bring your foot up towards your bottom, keeping your back straight and knees together
why: loosens the front of the thigh after prolonged sitting
restrictions: use desk/chair for balance; standing must be allowed

name: Posture self-check
instruction: Check: head and neck balanced, shoulders relaxed, wrists in line, lower back supported, and feet supported
why: notices the current setup without a camera

name: Seated chin tuck
instruction: While sitting, carefully pull your chin straight back without changing your eye level, holding for a few seconds
why: quick postural reset without leaving your seat

name: Wall posture check
instruction: Stand with your back against a wall so the back of your head, shoulder blades, hips, and back of your legs all touch it, and notice where your posture differs from that
why: notices postural drift without needing a camera
